correctness.rationale: The two-pulse model is precisely normalized. The baseline maximum is beta+exp(-delta) because beta>=1. The modified impulse is a convolution of two exponential reservoir kernels. The exponent-weighted derivative of the postarrival discharge is strictly decreasing, proving uniqueness of its maximizer. A piecewise envelope derivative proves the lag crossover for every positive rate; the harmful excess has an exact single maximizer at twice the routed mode, and u*coth(u)>=1 proves the rate-uniform e^(-2) bound and unique equality case. Boundary values r=1, delta=0 and beta=1 are included. The standalone standard-library checker supplied in this package independently checks 280478 finite assertions including exact-rational cases; finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The already recognized risk that local detention can increase downstream flood peaks is turned into an all-rate actionable mathematical benchmark: a necessary-and-sufficient arrival-lag boundary, robust independence from the strength of the later tributary, a unique worst-delay identity, and a universal optimal upper bound with its unique extremizer. This is not merely a numerical counterexample or an arbitrary parameter slice; it resolves the exact optimal risk envelope within a natural two-tributary routing model. The narrow scope limits empirical applications but does not eliminate the structural utility.
